decisions.reason: Requiring full through-hole pin access does not change the established GPIO assignments or compatibility rules.
The breakout and platform-reuse decision does not change I2C pull-ups, series resistors, bus speed, or signal conditioning.
The reference to a reusable platform with buttons does not alter the specified BOOT button, reset connection, or capacitance.
The parenthetical mention of buttons as a possible reuse case does not change the current panel-input assignments or mounting.
Generic ESP32-S3 platform reuse and full pin access do not change the standalone USB power requirement.
The source preserves the breakout despite routing pressure but does not establish a new board dimension, component position, or confirmed hole pitch; the 1.27 mm pitch is only proposed as a question.
The breakout and reuse decision does not alter the monitored rails, measurement coverage, or monitoring IC.
Reusing the board as a generic ESP32-S3 platform does not modify the established USB-C programming interface.
Full ESP32 pin breakout does not necessarily change any interboard connector, pinout, or board power topology.
The source does not change the panel-mounted power-button connector or its PWRON behavior.
The generic base-platform rationale does not change the separate sensor-board connector inventory or pinouts.
The ESP32 breakout decision has no necessary effect on the AXP2101 battery and USB power path.
